upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Great! I'll help you check your eligibility for Child Benefit. To get started, I need to ask you some questions about your child.

**First question: How old is your child?**

This is important because:
- Children **under 16** automatically qualify (subject to other conditions)
- Children **aged 16-19** may qualify if they're in approved education or training
- Children **aged 20 or over** generally don't qualify

Please tell me your child's age, or if you have multiple children, let's start with one child at a time.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Thanks for your help. I'm asking about my son Alex - he's 17 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're asking about your son Alex who is 17 years old.

Since Alex is 17 (which falls in the 16-19 age range), he may still qualify for Child Benefit, but we need to check if he meets certain education or training requirements.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Is Alex currently in education or training, or has he recently left education?**

Please tell me which of these applies:

1. **He's currently in approved education or training** (like A-levels, Scottish Highers, NVQs, or other approved courses)

2. **He recently left education or training** (within the last few months)

3. **Neither** - he's not in education/training and didn't recently leave

Which situation best describes Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's not in any education or training at the moment - he left school and isn't doing any courses right now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for clarifying. Since Alex left education or training, I need to check if he might still be eligible under an extension period.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Important question about the extension period:**

There's a special 20-week extension period available for young people aged 16-17 who have recently left education or training. To qualify for this extension, Alex would need to have:

1. **Left approved education or training within the last 20 weeks**, AND
2. **Registered with one of these services:**
   - A government careers service
   - Connexions (careers service)
   - The armed services

**When did Alex leave education, and has he registered with any of these services?**

Please note: This extension ends either after 20 weeks from leaving education OR when he turns 18, whichever comes first.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't registered with any careers service or anything like that. He just left school and hasn't signed up with Connexions or the armed forces or any of those services.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that information. Since Alex hasn't registered with any of the qualifying services (careers service, Connexions, or armed forces), he wouldn't be eligible for the 20-week extension period.

conversation.text:
## Child Benefit Eligibility Decision

I'm sorry, but based on the information you've provided, **you are not currently eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

### Why this decision was made:

For children aged 16-19, Child Benefit only continues if they are:
- In approved education or training, OR
- Eligible for a 20-week extension period after leaving education

Since Alex:
- Is 17 years old and has left school
- Is not currently in any approved education or training
- Has not registered with a qualifying service (government careers service, Connexions, or armed services)

He does not meet the requirements for Child Benefit to continue.

### What you could do:

1. **If Alex returns to education or training**: If Alex enrolls in approved education or training (such as A-levels, NVQs, Scottish Highers, or other approved courses), he may become eligible again. You would need to notify the Child Benefit Office.

2. **Register with a careers service**: If Alex registers with Connexions or a government careers service soon after leaving education, this could potentially activate the 20-week extension (though timing is important).

3. **For more information**: You can visit [https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/eligibility](https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/eligibility) or contact the Child Benefit Office if your circumstances change.

I understand this may be disappointing news. If you have any questions or if Alex's situation changes, please don't hesitate to reach out.
